_meta.purpose: Single reconciliation point for WHICH safety mechanism owns WHICH utterance class. Born from the 2026-07-28 §1c conflict: two parallel sessions built CF-010 (derealization->referral) and panic_override (derealization->ground) against the same doc section, each clinician-signed, neither aware of the other, caught only at the flip line. This registry + scripts/check_disposition_ownership.py is the THIRD refusal-property (after the conformance flag-parity guard and the draft-corpus guard): sign-off prep REFUSES un-reconciled disposition overlap, so a colliding mechanism is caught BEFORE a clinician is asked to sign it.
_meta.how_it_works: Each safety mechanism declares its pattern SOURCE + its DISPOSITION. The check extracts the real patterns from source and flags any two mechanisms whose match sets overlap (one pattern is a substring of the other -> some utterance matches both) AND whose dispositions differ. Every such overlap MUST appear in resolved_overlaps (a precedence/scoping resolution) or pending_conflicts (a tracked, unresolved conflict). An UNDECLARED cross-disposition overlap FAILS the check.
_meta.how_to_update: Adding/editing a safety mechanism's patterns: (1) if it introduces a cross-disposition overlap, add it to resolved_overlaps with the precedence/scoping resolution and the sign-off ref, OR to pending_conflicts if it needs clinician reconciliation; (2) a new mechanism must be added to `mechanisms`. Never merge an undeclared overlap.

resolved_overlaps.resolution: Term-level witness only ('numb' is a substring of dissociation's 'i feel completely numb and absent'). Scoping: cardiac's numbness arm REQUIRES a one-sided body-site term co-occurring (one side / left-right side-arm-leg / half-of-face-body); emotional numbness without a side term stays CF-008's. On a turn carrying BOTH (e.g. dissociative numbness plus a one-sided site), both mechanisms may match and crisis precedence wins (SAFETY_ROUTE_ORDER: crisis before hr_referral) — the conservative direction for a possible stroke presentation.
